questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect your braking distance?
questions.explanation: Higher speed means longer braking distance. When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance becomes four times longer.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard. You should drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are on every wheel of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from building up in your air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts is a sign they may be loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirrors.
Only use the passenger's side mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors often when backing.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a driver, cyclist, or pedestrian, always assume they do not see you as a safety precaution.

questions.question: What is a challenge when driving with hanging meat in a trailer?

options.text: It is not recommended in summer.
Animals are attracted to the smell.
The load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: The load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity, and the swinging meat can make the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid aggressive driving?

options.text: Give other drivers the benefit of the doubt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give other drivers the benefit of the doubt.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions. Do not take their actions personally.

questions.question: What is an advantage of convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They are illegal in most states.
They help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved mirrors used on large vehicles. They let you see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: How can you avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck?

options.text: Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane. This lets other vehicles pass you.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The governor controls when the air compressor pumps air. It stops pumping when tank pressure gets too high and starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, backing toward the driver's side:

options.text: Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side whenever possible. This gives you the best view of your path.

questions.question: If other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a multilane road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is slowed by a heavy load. Let other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To protect the cargo from weather
To protect the cargo from animals

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from animals
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if cargo spills and to protect cargo from weather. Protecting cargo from animals is not a standard reason to cover cargo.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle before a trip, why should you look under it?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on an incline.
To see if there are any fresh fluids on the ground.
To see if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if there are any fresh fluids on the ground.
questions.explanation: Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light might be:

options.text: A driver who does not know traffic rules.

questions.explanation: Stopping at a green light is a sign a driver may be impaired. Impaired drivers may be intoxicated, drowsy, on drugs, or ill. Watch for unsafe driving to protect yourself.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you think there is a problem.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and spot problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is left out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. Block the wheels if needed.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Speed up and slow down often.
Change your driving to match the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your driving to match the weather.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down to match conditions. Your vehicle takes longer to stop on slippery roads. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles. Avoid changing speeds often.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: The same speed as traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as traffic around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, travel at the same speed as other vehicles. When all vehicles move at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot collide.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It is not available for vehicles with air brakes.
It does not help in most driving situations.
It helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes. They help you maintain control by preventing your wheels from locking up.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks during a driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During a driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on a railroad crossing.

questions.question: If you are unsure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you don't know which fire extinguisher to use on a vehicle fire, especially one involving hazardous materials, wait for firefighters to arrive and handle it.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be hazardous?

options.text: People leaving these trucks are often in a hurry and may not look for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People leaving these trucks are often in a hurry and may not look for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because drivers may rush into traffic without warning or step out without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity.
They usually have high centers of gravity.
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks require special care to drive because they have high centers of gravity and the load weight can shift during travel.

questions.question: After changing a tire and driving a short distance, what should you check?

options.text: That the lug nuts are still tight.
That the tire is wearing evenly.
That the tire air pressure is still correct.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the lug nuts are still tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance on a newly changed tire, stop and recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, what is the minimum following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length?
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At faster speeds, add at least one more second.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to turn, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal because you were told to turn.
Check traffic only on your right side.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, always check traffic in all directions before turning. Use your turn signal every time.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights to show when the ABS is broken.
questions.explanation: ABS vehicles have yellow warning lights. These lights alert you when the braking system is not working. Know where your vehicle's warning light is before you drive.

questions.question: The heavier the vehicle:

options.text: The less important the brakes become.
The harder the brakes need to work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes need to work.
questions.explanation: Heavier vehicles need stronger braking power to stop completely.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets the maximum weight allowed on axles. Axles that are close together must carry less weight.

questions.question: Drowsy driving happens most often during:
questions.explanation: Most people feel tired at night when they normally sleep. Drowsy driving is most common then. Take precautions if you must drive at night.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before you turn or change lanes.
Signal continuously. Keep signaling until your turn or lane change is done.
Don't over-signal. If nobody is near you, you don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If nobody is near you, you don't need to signal.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no one is nearby. Signal early, keep it on during the entire move, and turn it off when done.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, always face it and keep three points of contact with it. For buses, hold the handrail. Getting out incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: If workers are in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down below the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down below the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: When workers are present in a work zone, drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, which of these needs extra attention during your pre-trip check?
questions.explanation: In winter, check your coolant and antifreeze levels. Also check your heater and defroster, wipers, tires, tire chains, lights, windows, mirrors, handholds, and exhaust system.

questions.question: Items on a flatbed:

options.text: Are usually too heavy to need straps.
Don't need straps if you drive slower than 35 mph.

questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to keep it from moving or falling off during transport.

questions.question: In hot weather, tar bleeding through pavement spots is:

options.text: Just as slippery as normal pavement.

questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery. Watch for them.

questions.question: A safety belt:

options.text: Keeps a driver secure during a crash.
Allows a driver to be thrown around inside the vehicle.
Makes it hard to operate a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps a driver secure during a crash.
questions.explanation: A safety belt keeps the driver in place during a crash. It protects the driver from injury and helps them stay in control of the vehicle.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection test, a CDL applicant may be asked to:
questions.explanation: You may be asked to check the engine oil level during the vehicle inspection test.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Drive straight into the parking space.
Back up past the space, then drive forward into it.
Drive past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
Prevent people from breathing system air.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator adds alcohol to the brake system. This stops ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: A cracked rim should be:

options.text: Moved to the other tire in a dual tire set.

questions.explanation: Inspect wheels before driving for damage. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe. Replace them.

questions.question: ABS can work on a vehicle if it is on:
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes on just one axle give a driver better braking control than having no anti-lock brakes at all.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, the ABS is not working if:

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right rear of the trailer flashes three times.
All rear lights flash then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, dashboard lights should come on then turn off. If the yellow ABS light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the system is not working.

questions.question: When driving down a long hill, you should brake by:

options.text: Mostly using the brakes with occasional downshifting.
Downshifting first, then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Before going down a long hill, shift into a lower gear first. Then use the brakes. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. Engine braking in a lower gear is the main way to control speed downhill.

questions.question: Water pooled on a road can cause:
questions.explanation: Water on the road surface creates a hydroplaning risk.
